title: 12-Lead ECG
author: G. Marsh, MD
summary: Sinus tachycardia 114, PR 148 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 432 ms (Bazett), axis +35. Horizontal ST depression 1.5 mm in V4-V6 (0.5 mm in I and aVL, 0.5 mm downsloping in V3) with T-wave inversion V5-V6; no ST elevation (0.5 mm reciprocal change in aVR). Lateral subendocardial ischemia pattern.
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 114 bpm. PR 148 ms. QRS 88 ms. QTc 432 ms (Bazett). Axis +35 degrees.

**Interpretation**
Sinus tachycardia, regular, no ectopy. Inferior leads: isoelectric ST, normal T waves, no pathological Q waves. V1-V3: normal R-wave progression, isoelectric ST in V1-V2 and a subtle 0.5 mm downsloping ST depression in V3. **V4-V6, I and aVL: 1.5 mm horizontal ST depression in V4, V5 and V6 (0.5 mm in I and aVL) with symmetric T-wave inversion in V5-V6**: acute subendocardial lateral-wall ischemia in the first obtuse marginal territory. No ST elevation in any lead (0.5 mm benign reciprocal change in aVR).

**Context**
Epigastric ache with sweating and fatigue for 36 hours, deep breathing, glucose HIGH on the meter; labs and the first troponin are pending. This is an NSTE-ACS pattern: aspirin given, serial troponin and cardiology to follow.
impression: Sinus tachycardia 114 with 1.5 mm ST depression V4-V6 and T inversion V5-V6: NSTE-ACS pattern. QTc 432 ms.

title: 12-Lead ECG
author: W. Haldane, MD
summary: Sinus rhythm 96 with frequent unifocal ventricular premature beats (left ventricular origin, right bundle branch block pattern, QRS 136 ms; about 7 per minute with couplets and trigeminal runs) near the end of the T-U wave. PR 164 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 492 ms (T-U fusion). Diffuse T-wave flattening with prominent U waves; persistent 1.0 mm ST depression V4-V6. Hypokalemia pattern (potassium 3.3) on top of lateral ischemia.
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 96 bpm. PR 164 ms. QRS 92 ms (136 ms on the premature beats). QTc 492 ms (Bazett; the T and U waves are fused, so this is a QTc/QUc). Axis +30 degrees.

**Interpretation**
Sinus rhythm with **frequent unifocal ventricular premature beats** (left ventricular origin, right bundle branch block morphology; about 7 per minute, with couplets and trigeminal runs) that fall near the end of the T-U wave: R-on-T risk. Inferior leads: diffuse T-wave flattening with U waves visible after the T in lead II. V1-V3: markedly flattened T waves with **prominent upright U waves (over 1.5 mm in V2-V3, taller than the T wave)**. V4-V6, I and aVL: persistent 1.0 mm horizontal ST depression, flattened T waves, U waves in V4-V5. Compared with 0140: rate slower (114 to 96), ST depression smaller (1.5 to 1.0 mm), new U waves and ventricular ectopy.

**Context**
Potassium 3.3 on the 0655 specimen (released 0710) on an insulin infusion in an acute NSTEMI. Ventricular ectopy on an ischemic myocardium with hypokalemia can degenerate into polymorphic ventricular tachycardia: hold the insulin, replace potassium (peripheral limit 10 mEq/h), keep K at 4.0 or higher and magnesium normal, and keep him on telemetry.
impression: Sinus rhythm 96, frequent unifocal PVCs, flat T with prominent U waves, ST depression 1.0 mm V4-V6 at potassium 3.3. QTc 492 ms (T-U fusion).

title: 12-Lead ECG
author: A. Vogt, MD
summary: Sinus rhythm 94, PR 156 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 438 ms (Bazett). Horizontal ST depression 1.5 mm in V4-V6 (deeper than 1.0 mm at 0715), T-wave inversion V5-V6; no ventricular ectopy and no U waves (potassium 4.1 at 1115). Recurrent lateral ischemia with chest pressure.
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 94 bpm. PR 156 ms. QRS 90 ms. QTc 438 ms (Bazett).

**Interpretation**
Sinus rhythm. **1.5 mm horizontal ST depression in V4-V6 with T-wave inversion in V5-V6**, deeper than the 1.0 mm on the 0715 tracing. No premature beats, no U waves, narrow QRS. No ST elevation.

**Context**
Recorded at 1405 during new 5/10 retrosternal and epigastric pressure, 15 minutes before the sublingual nitroglycerin was given. Potassium 4.1 at 1115, so the ectopy and U waves have gone. Recurrent angina from the culprit lateral lesion: continue heparin and aspirin, repeat troponin with the next panel, and review after the nitrate.
impression: Sinus rhythm 94 with 1.5 mm ST depression V4-V6 and T inversion V5-V6 during chest pressure: recurrent lateral ischemia. No ectopy. QTc 438 ms.

title: 12-Lead ECG
author: W. Haldane, MD
summary: Sinus rhythm 68, PR 160 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 418 ms (Bazett), axis +32. Complete resolution of the lateral ST depression in V4-V6; upright T in V4-V5, trace flattening in V6; U waves gone; no premature beats. Compatible with reperfusion of the first obtuse marginal after stenting.
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 68 bpm. PR 160 ms. QRS 86 ms. QTc 418 ms (Bazett). Axis +32 degrees.

**Interpretation**
Normal sinus rhythm, completely regular, no premature atrial or ventricular beats. Inferior leads: isoelectric ST, normal T. V1-V3: isoelectric ST, normal T-wave amplitude, **U waves gone**. **V4-V6, I and aVL: complete resolution of the horizontal ST depression** (isoelectric), upright T in V4-V5 with only trace flattening in V6. Compared with 1405 yesterday and 0140: resolved.

**Context**
Post drug-eluting stent to the first obtuse marginal (right radial, completed about 1215). Potassium 4.3 at 0700. Telemetry can continue.
impression: Normal sinus rhythm 68. Lateral ST depression resolved, no U waves, no ectopy. QTc 418 ms.
